title: Khadijah's caravan
hook: she sends him to Syria with her goods and her servant Maysarah, who returns full of praise

segments.voice: Yesterday, the trustworthy. Your line was: known for truth. When your hard moment came, did you say the true sentence? That closes the childhood and youth. Now, a new part: Khadijah and the household. Day seven hundred sixteen.
screen: `KNOWN FOR TRUTH.` → `NOW: KHADIJAH AND THE HOUSEHOLD.`

segments.voice: A merchant in Mecca has goods to send north, and she doesn't travel with them. Whoever carries them will be out of her sight for a long time, buying and selling with her money in markets far from Mecca. She needs someone she can trust completely, someone who will bring back every coin, and she has heard a name. The merchant is a woman, Khadijah bint Khuwaylid. Today: Khadijah's caravan.
screen: `GOODS TO SEND NORTH.` → `OUT OF HER SIGHT FOR A LONG TIME.` → `A WOMAN OF TRADE.`

segments.voice: Ibn Ishaq describes Khadijah as a merchant woman of honor and wealth, who hired men to trade with her goods for a share of the profit. She has heard about the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: his truthfulness, his trustworthiness, his character. Yesterday's title has traveled. So she sends him an offer. Take my goods to Syria, she says, and I'll give you more than I give the others. And she sends her servant Maysarah with him. He accepts. The caravan goes north. He trades, sells what he brought, buys what she wanted, and comes back to Mecca. The sirah says the business did well. But the profit isn't what the story lingers on. It lingers on Maysarah. Maysarah has spent the whole journey beside him, seeing him far from home: in the heat, at the market, at the haggling table where small dishonesties are easy. When they return, Maysarah goes to Khadijah and tells her what he saw. Ibn Ishaq says his report included wonders: a monk's words about him, and angels Maysarah saw shading him from the sun. That's the turn in this story. The goods came back. So did a report, and it was about the man, not the profit. The Qur'an's word for something handed over like this is amanah, a trust. In surah four, Pickthall translates: "Lo! Allah commandeth you that ye restore deposits to their owners." He restored hers, and more. Later, in a hadith collected by al-Tirmidhi, the Prophet says the truthful, trustworthy merchant will be with the prophets, the truthful and the martyrs. A merchant, in that company. Tomorrow we'll see what Khadijah did with Maysarah's report.
screen: `A MERCHANT WOMAN OF HONOR.` · `"TAKE MY GOODS TO SYRIA."` · `MAYSARAH WATCHES THE WHOLE WAY.` · `THE REPORT WAS ABOUT HIM.` · then, large: `RESTORE DEPOSITS TO THEIR OWNERS.`

segments.voice: The practice: do work you'd be glad to be reported on. Settle, and breathe. Bring to mind one piece of work you'll do today, paid or unpaid: a task at your job, a chore, an errand for someone, an assignment. Now picture a Maysarah beside you, someone quiet, simply watching how you do it. Not to catch you out; just to see. What would they report? Is there one corner you'd usually cut, one shortcut nobody would notice? Choose, now, to do that part well. If you pray, you can ask Allah for honest hands. If not, just hold the choice. The bell holds the time.
Khadijah's caravan. The trading journey to Syria she entrusted to him, with her servant Maysarah, who came home, the sirah says, speaking of him with wonder. Today's word.
Your line: his honesty was the report. Today, do the corner you'd usually cut, properly, whether or not anyone ever finds out. Day seven hundred sixteen.

howItsDone: Muslims remember Khadijah as a respected merchant and as the Prophet's ﷺ first wife, and honesty in trade is taught from his example and from hadith such as the one on the truthful, trustworthy merchant.

fork.setup: you're Khadijah. your goods will be out of your sight for a long time. you've heard of a young man called the trustworthy. what do you do?
options: hire him, offer him more, and send Maysarah along.
fork.reveal: the sirah says she offered him more than others, and sent her servant Maysarah with him.

original.note: Arabic: amanah, a trust, something placed in your keeping to be returned.

trapdoor: what you thought: a business trip before the love story.
what it means: she trusted him with her goods, and the report that came back was about his honesty.
what a scholar hears: Ibn Ishaq on Khadijah's terms and Maysarah's report; 4:58 on returning trusts; al-Tirmidhi on the trustworthy merchant.

sources.ref: Ibn Ishaq, Sirat Rasul Allah (Khadijah sends him to Syria with her goods and Maysarah; Maysarah's report)

notes: This day opens a new part (Khadijah and the household); the review names the turn. Confirm.
Ibn Ishaq's further details (the monk under the tree, Maysarah seeing two angels shade him) are now mentioned in one sentence, without retelling the monk scene from day 713.

Editor: the teach had said Maysarah's report 'was about his character', but Ibn Ishaq's report is about a monk's words and angels shading him; the teach now says so and keeps the point that the report was about the man, not the profit. Also cut 'with no one from Mecca watching' (Maysarah was himself from Mecca) and the hook's sweeping 'a problem every owner of goods has'.
The caravan's duration is not stated.
Pickthall 4:58 quoted from memory; confirm wording.
Tirmidhi 1209 number and grading (hasan) cited from memory; confirm.
Ages of Khadijah and the Prophet, and the size of the profit, are left out under the claims rule.

Auditor: the hook said she 'can't go' with her goods and that the markets were ones 'she will never see'; Ibn Ishaq says only that she hired men to trade for her. Now 'she doesn't travel with them' and 'markets far from Mecca'.
